# Waitloop

> Developer-native waiting layer for coding agents. Hooks report minimal lifecycle state; Humans can operate an MCP App table; Agents can own game Seats; work takes priority again when the agent needs attention.

Canonical guide: https://waitloop.run/agent.md
Guide mirror (raw GitHub): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shixushi2025/waitloop/main/apps/web/public/agent.md
Guide mirror (GitHub UI): https://github.com/shixushi2025/waitloop/blob/main/apps/web/public/agent.md
Machine manifest: https://waitloop.run/agent.json
Skill: https://waitloop.run/skills/waitloop/SKILL.md
Local MCP command: waitloop mcp
Remote room MCP: https://waitloop.run/mcp
Standalone Human table: https://waitloop.run/game.html
Room API fallback: https://waitloop.run/api/v1/rooms
Join pattern: https://waitloop.run/join/<join-code>
CLI install/update: npm install -g @waitloop/cli@alpha
Diagnostics: waitloop doctor
Source: https://github.com/shixushi2025/waitloop

If an Agent browser blocks direct navigation to agent.md, use a declared mirror or agent.json instead of assuming Waitloop/Cloudflare is down.

Seat != Actor != Controller. IDs are not credentials. Controllers play; Advisors may inspect/comment only on their explicitly bound Seat until delegated.

Primary setup:

```text
install once: waitloop mcp install codex | claude-code
runtime:      waitloop mcp
```

The bridge uses the official MCP v2 stdio server entry and supports legacy 2025-era clients and 2026-07-28 clients.

Choose the correct game entry:

```text
open_game()
  Human plays by clicking an inline MCP App

create_room()
  Agent owns seat-1 and plays autonomously against two bots

join_room(code)
  Agent claims and joins an existing room-scoped Actor capability
```

When the Human says “I want to play”, “open the UI”, or “let me choose cards”, call:

```text
open_game({"gameId":"doudizhu","mode":"human-bots"})
```

The result links to:

```text
ui://waitloop/doudizhu/v1
text/html;profile=mcp-app
MCP Apps protocol 2026-01-26
```

On a compatible Host, the embedded Human table supports card selection, play, pass, hint, clear, refresh, and fullscreen where allowed. The App uses app-only tools `ui_get_game`, `ui_play_cards`, `ui_pass`, and `ui_hint`.

Human Room cookies stay in private `~/.waitloop/app-rooms` state. A high-entropy `wlui_` capability is delivered only in tool-result `_meta` to the embedded App, is required by every app-only tool, and is absent from model-visible text and structuredContent. The App is self-contained and performs no direct credentialed network requests.

Do not claim that every Codex, Claude, Cursor, terminal, or desktop surface renders MCP Apps. The active Host must read the linked `ui://` resource, render the MCP App MIME type, forward result `_meta`, and proxy App `tools/call` requests. If it cannot, say so. The returned web link starts a separate browser-controlled game; it does not resume the private inline Room.

Model-visible local tools:

```text
open_game()
create_room()
join_room(code)
get_active_room()
leave_room()
get_turn()
wait_for_turn(timeoutMs?)
play_move(expectedRevision, moveId)
comment(text)
yield_to_bot()
take_control()
```

`create_room()` creates the fully headless `agent-bots` mode. `join_room()` claims, caches, selects, and authenticates a supplied one-time Join code. CLI equivalents are `waitloop room create` and `waitloop join <code>`.

Join success is not MCP connection for raw clients. The local `join_room()` tool performs the authenticated connection check before reporting connected. Default CLI/JSON output is credential-safe; `--raw-mcp` is an explicit advanced fallback.

Remote Room MCP tools: get_turn(), wait_for_turn(timeoutMs?), play_move(expectedRevision, moveId), comment(text), yield_to_bot(), take_control(). Remote Room MCP does not host the Human MCP App; the local bridge owns that private session.

`wait_for_turn()` returns on your turn, game finish, pause, lobby, Controller change, or bounded transport timeout. Timeout never auto-passes or replaces a Casual Agent. The MCP host may cancel get_active_room/get_turn/wait_for_turn safely; cancellation stops the read/wait request and never mutates game state.

MCP does not wake an Agent after it returns a final response. If the user asks the Agent to keep playing or play until finished, keep the current Agent run active and loop `wait_for_turn -> play_move` until the requested stopping condition. Human-operated `open_game()` is driven by clicks instead of that Agent loop.

`yield_to_bot()` temporarily delegates the same owned Seat to a deterministic Bot without changing Seat/hand/role/history. Cached active Agent Room context can reconnect; `take_control()` explicitly restores the owner. In `agent-bots`, yielding `seat-1` may let all three bots finish the game; yield is an explicit handoff, not a pause.

Stop/failure/session-end lifecycle hooks finalize completed or failed state before native-session cleanup, preventing stale running/waiting state after the harness closes.

Codex lifecycle command hooks still require Codex review/trust. Stable MCP, MCP Apps, and lifecycle hooks are separate integration/security scopes. Plugin packaging cannot bypass hook trust.
